h: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ סִיוָן, א׳ Rosh Chodesh Sivan, 1

p: It is stated in Sefer Yetzirah,
according to the version of the Arizal:
"He crowned the letter zayin in walking," etc.,
"and the left foot in the soul."
the time of the receiving of the Torah,
"Fortunate are those whose way is perfect,
who walk in the Torah of Hashem,"
But what connection does the left foot have
to the matter of receiving the Torah?
However, one can say regarding this,
along the lines of the saying of Chazal
"and it stands to reason that the good one is at his right," etc.,
'The heart of a wise man is at his right,
and the heart of a fool at his left.'"
That is, the counsel for external matters,
for the needs of the body,
And it is stated in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 35:1)
and turned my feet back to Your testimonies":
'I am going to such-and-such a place,'
and my feet would bring me
to batei knessiyos and batei midrashos."
had the words of Torah become fixed in his heart
which are of the aspect of the left foot,
there came from this itself a right,
"'I did not toil, yet I found' — do not believe it,"
of the contradiction within the expression "I toiled and I found":
רַק שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַיְגִיעָה הַרְבֵּה מִקּוֹדֶם
only that through much toil beforehand
by way of a find, unexpectedly.
And to this one can apply the expression
So what is the expression "and I turned back,"
from which it appears that he turned them back?
so that they would now turn back by themselves
And to this the left foot alludes:
even the walking of the left
is likewise turned to the right,
And the version of the Geonim:
"He crowned the letter zayin in smell," etc.,
the allusion to acquiring words of Torah,
comes through purity of the soul
from the impurity that issues from the body,
"Purity nullified the taste and the smell," etc.;
"I smell the scent of a chinunisa" —
אָמַר לוֹ: בְּנִי, טָהֳרָה יֵשׁ בְּךָ.
he said to him, "My son, there is purity in you."
And certainly what is meant is not merely
purity from the tumah of the body,
for at that time there was no longer in effect
וְגַם לֹא הָיָה לָהֶם אֵפֶר פָּרָה
nor did they have the ashes of the parah
It is also stated in the Gemara (Eruvin 21b)
these are the young men of Yisrael
who have not tasted the taste of sin.
at the time of childhood and youth,
שֶׁאָז הַיֵּצֶר הָרַע שֶׁל תַּאֲוָה מִתְגַּבֵּר.
when the yetzer hara of desire grows strong.
And then, when one guards himself in this
he is the vessel prepared for receiving the Torah,
which is acquired in the soul through yiras Shamayim,
"The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem."
And this is the aspect of smell,
"And He will imbue him with a sense of the fear of Hashem,"
this is one who learns Torah in purity," etc.
well known is the saying of Chazal (Berachos 61b),
yet in the Zohar HaKadosh it is evident
that from the spleen sadness is born in a person,
"the sadness of the spleen and the anger of the gall."
for one is set against the other:
regarding the laughter of the fool,
that is, the joy of frivolity,
from it are born sadness and melancholy,
that it brings wailing and sadness in the end.
And this is the root of the serpent's enticement
that it brought sorrow into the heart of man,
"In sorrow you shall eat of it," etc.;
it brings laxity into the heart
toward the pursuit of avodas Hashem.
However, the laughter and the joy
through "the fear of Hashem is pure"
one comes to "the precepts of Hashem are upright,
as in "my joy is from within my fear"
And the matter of the letter zayin
יֵשׁ לוֹ גַּם כֵּן שַׁיָּיכוּת לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
also has a connection to Matan Torah,
as stated in the Midrash (Shemos Rabbah 30:3):
with weapons on this side and weapons on that side
so too the Torah — judgments on this side," etc.
For the Torah comes from the side of Gevurah
and from the side of Yitzchak
דְּכֵן הוּא נִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם הַצְּחוֹק,
for indeed he is named for laughter,
and as it says in the Midrash
that there was much laughter in the world,
וְכֵן בְּמִדְרָשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם [חֵלֶק א קכט, א]] —
and so too in the Midrash HaNe'lam (Zohar I, 129a) —
Only through the power of the Torah
as stated in the Zohar HaKadosh
"and He shone forth from Seir to them":
that we were given the power of the sword
"and Who is the sword of your majesty."
And specifically to subdue his own side,
"Their sword shall enter their own heart," etc.
And this is as it says (ibid. 149:6),
"and a double-edged sword in their hand,
to execute vengeance upon the nations," etc.
And this is "the weapons on this side and on that side,"
like the shape of the letter zayin
And this is the connection of the letter zayin as well
the time of the receiving of the Torah.
